links.comparator_used: Full original anonymized medical reports (lengthy, unstructured) as input, versus manually generated case summaries
links.outcome: Agreement with heart team treatment decision (Cohen κ), reliability (ICC), and bias toward TAVR (FBI)
links.effect: Original reports: κ -0.47 to 0.22; ICC 0.0-1.0; FBI 0.95-1.51. Case summaries plus added guideline knowledge: κ -0.02 to 0.63; ICC 0.01-1.0; FBI 0.46-1.23. The summary and guideline effects are not separated.
links.tradeoff: Summaries were manually generated, which is a curation burden. Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs tested, and the authors conclude that advanced LLMs still require extensively curated input.
links.quote: The LLMs' performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (Cohen κ coefficient: -0.02 to 0.63; ICC: 0.01-1.0; FBI: 0.46-1.23).

links.comparator_used: Prompt without added guideline knowledge, applied to original medical reports
links.outcome: Agreement with heart team treatment decision (Cohen κ), reliability (ICC), and bias toward TAVR (FBI)
links.effect: Original reports: κ -0.47 to 0.22; ICC 0.0-1.0; FBI 0.95-1.51. Case summaries plus guideline knowledge in the prompt: κ -0.02 to 0.63; ICC 0.01-1.0; FBI 0.46-1.23. The guideline effect is confounded with the switch to summaries.
links.tradeoff: Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs tested. Reliability remained variable (ICC 0.01-1.0), and some models still agreed poorly with the heart team (κ as low as -0.02).
links.quote: The LLMs' performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (Cohen κ coefficient: -0.02 to 0.63; ICC: 0.01-1.0; FBI: 0.46-1.23).
